title: Game Development
blurb: Engines, the game loop, vectors and transforms, rendering, physics, game AI, gameplay architecture, design and optimisation.

quiz.question: Why multiply movement by delta time?
options: So speed is consistent regardless of frame rate
quiz.explanation: Per-frame movement would vary with FPS.

quiz.question: How can you test whether an enemy is in front of the player?
options: Dot product of forward and direction to enemy > 0 (or > cos(half FOV))
quiz.explanation: Dot product measures alignment of directions.

quiz.question: Why do engines store rotations as quaternions?
options: Avoid gimbal lock and interpolate smoothly
quiz.explanation: Euler angles suffer gimbal lock and poor interpolation.

quiz.question: A mobile game has 900 draw calls. What usually helps most?
options: Batching via sprite/texture atlases and fewer materials
quiz.explanation: Draw call overhead is a common CPU bottleneck.

quiz.question: What is coyote time?
options: A short grace period to jump after leaving a ledge
quiz.explanation: Small tolerances make controls feel fair.

quiz.question: Which algorithm is standard for pathfinding on a graph or navmesh?
quiz.explanation: A* uses cost-so-far plus a heuristic.

quiz.question: Why use object pooling for bullets?
options: Avoid allocation and garbage-collection spikes from frequent create/destroy
quiz.explanation: Reuse objects instead of instantiating each frame.

quiz.question: Where should you profile a mobile game?
quiz.explanation: Editor and desktop performance are misleading.

problems.title: Fix a stuttering mobile game
problems.prompt: A mobile game hitches every few seconds. Diagnose and fix.
problems.solution: Profile on device to find periodic spikes; check GC allocations (strings, LINQ, instantiation), asset loading on main thread, expensive periodic logic; fix with pooling, allocation-free hot paths, async loading, time-slicing; verify with profiler against budgets.
